1.explanation:
All of these files participate in generating the dropdown’s markup and ARIA attributes:

• packages/components/src/components/dropdown/dropdown.config.js defines the HTML template for the vanilla JS dropdown, including the id suffix (`__menu`).
• packages/components/src/components/dropdown/dropdown.js instantiates that template and wires up aria-owns/aria-controls using the same id suffix.
• packages/react/src/components/Dropdown/Dropdown.js is the React wrapper that passes `id`, renders the label, the field, and the menu, and sets aria-label (currently hard-coded to “open menu”). It inherits the double-underscore menu id from the vanilla layer.
• packages/react/src/components/Dropdown/Dropdown.Skeleton.js does the same markup in its skeleton state.

To correct the violations you need to:
1. Change the menu id suffix from `__menu` to something ARIA-friendly (e.g. `-menu`) in both dropdown.config.js and dropdown.js.  
2. Update the React component to use the new id convention and to build its accessible name (via aria-label or aria-labelledby) so it includes the visible label text.  

Those four files are where you’ll implement both fixes.
1.bug_scenario:
When you render the Carbon React Dropdown example and open the menu, the DOM shows a button with
…
DAP reports two failures: 1. “ARIA attributes must conform to valid values” — it flags the id value `carbon-dropdown-example__menu` in aria-owns/aria-controls as invalid (the double-underscore suffix). 2. “Accessible name does not contain the visible label text” — the button’s aria-label (‘open menu’) doesn’t include the visible label (“This is not a dropdown title”).

2.explanation: Both of these files are responsible for generating the dropdown’s markup and wiring up its ARIA attributes. In packages/components/src/components/dropdown/dropdown.js the vanilla dropdown logic builds the menu’s id (appending “__menu”) and writes aria-owns/aria-controls on the toggle. In react/src/components/Dropdown/Dropdown.js the React wrapper similarly concatenates the user-supplied id plus “__menu” when it calls Downshift’s getMenuProps/getToggleButtonProps. Because the id on the actual menu element either isn’t rendered or doesn’t match exactly (and the double-underscore pattern falls outside what the ARIA IDREF rule allows), the aria references end up pointing at a non-existent or invalid id. Fixing how these files compute and assign a valid, matching id for the menu (and updating the corresponding aria-owns/aria-controls) will resolve the violations.
2.bug_scenario: In the React dropdown demo, the toggle button is rendered with aria-owns and aria-controls attributes set to “carbon-dropdown-example__menu”, but the menu container either doesn’t carry that exact id or the id syntax (double underscore naming) is not accepted as a valid ARIA identifier. As a result, both DAP and axe-core report “ARIA attributes must conform to valid values” (invalid aria-owns/aria-controls target) and “Certain ARIA roles must contain particular children” (the button’s accessible name doesn’t match the visible label).
